[A64] Use REV32 and ZIP for byte-order permutes and merges

PERMUTE by bytes (vperm) XORed every control byte with 3 to map PPC
byte indices onto the host's word-swapped layout, which needs the
control in a register and three extra instructions. Byte-reversing each
word of the two tables with REV32 does the same and doubles as the copy
into v0/v1: register controls go from 7 to 5 instructions. Constant
tables are swapped at emit time.

Constant merge controls get dedicated forms: vmrghb/vmrglb become
ZIP1/ZIP2 plus REV32 with no control vector to load, vmrghh/vmrglh ZIP
plus REV64.4S (2 instructions instead of 4), and vmrghw/vmrglw a single
ZIP1/ZIP2 (instead of 4).

The golden corpus covers vperm and every vmrg form.

Evidence, guest-loop microbenchmark (512M-1B iterations, final
registers cross-checked): vperm latency -66.2%, throughput -75.2%. No
title-level measurement.

[A64] Skip a same-register truncation that only compares read

TRUNCATE_I32_I64 into the register its source already occupies emits
mov wN, wN, whose only effect is clearing the upper half. That clearing
is needed in general: an I32 value's upper half being zero is what lets
ZERO_EXTEND_I64_I32 elide its own move. It is not needed when every
reader of the result is a compare, which reads it as a 32-bit operand,
so skip the move in that case. Only compares are accepted because they
are the readers this was checked for; a naive version that skipped the
move for every reader broke mulhwu.

Evidence: -29,639 emitted host instructions (-1.2%) on the Halo 3 menu
corpus. A replayed Halo 3 function ran -1.38% and -1.45% in the two A/B
orderings, against a same-binary control of -0.39%/+0.11%.

Remember the last texture found per key and the last view per texture

The texture of a fetch constant's key and the image view a draw samples it
through were looked up in hash tables at every use, though the draws of a
frame keep naming textures found shortly before and sample them the same
way. With texture_lookup_memo (on; debug.xendroid.lookup_memo), a
direct-mapped memo by key sits in front of the texture table (an entry is
dropped with its texture), and each texture remembers the arguments of its
last GetView and the view. Results are identical.

Command thread profiles (20 s, frame-time accounting off, POCO F7):
GetView 2.5 -> 0.5% of the samples in Red Dead Redemption, 2.7 -> 0.7% in
GTA IV; the texture table lookups 2.9 -> 2.6% and 3.8 -> 3.4% (the memo
included). The frame rate change is within the run-to-run noise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
